skills.whatToLearn: Hardware vs software, CPU/RAM/storage, operating systems, files/folders, extensions, installing programs, browsers, basic troubleshooting ; Computer hardware basics, CPU/processor, cores and threads, RAM, HDD vs SSD, storage capacity, motherboard basics, input/output devices, operating systems, Windows basics, Linux basics, files and folders, directory structure, absolute vs relative paths, file extensions, file permissions, users and administrator/root access, installing and uninstalling software, software versions,  applications vs processes, Task Manager/System Monitor, background services, command line/terminal, basic CMD/PowerShell/Bash commands, environment variables, PATH variable, text editors such as Notepad and Notepad++, code editors such as VS Code,  ZIP/unZIP and file compression, software packages and package managers, processes and memory usage, networking basics, LAN vs internet, IP address, private vs public IP, localhost, DNS, ports, TCP/IP basics, HTTP vs HTTPS, URLs, client-server architecture, request and response concept, APIs basics, JSON, CSV, XML basics, databases basics, tables/rows/columns, relational vs non-relational databases, SQL basics, data types, encoding such as UTF-8, Git and version control basics, GitHub basics, programming logic, variables, conditions, loops, functions, errors and exceptions, libraries and dependencies, logs and log files, authentication vs authorization, passwords and MFA, encryption basics, cybersecurity basics, backups, cloud computing basics, servers, virtual machines, containers/Docker basics, virtualization, cloud storage, local vs remote systems, SSH basics, remote connections, software development environments such as development/test/production, basic troubleshooting, reading error messages, checking CPU/RAM/disk/network usage, restarting processes/services, and understanding how code, APIs, servers, databases, storage, networks, and users all communicate with each other.
skills.depthComment: Must be strong. This is the foundation for everything else.
skills.mentorComments: Syed 9/19/26: This should already be partially completed as I gave some basic videos to watch  at Whatsapp group'

skills.whatToLearn: IP address, Wi-Fi, router, modem, LAN/WAN, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, ports, client/server, VPN
skills.depthComment: Only understand how computers communicate. No advanced networking yet.
skills.mentorComments: For this topicmake sure to ask me questions so I can send you some good latest concepts videos

skills.whatToLearn: Rows/columns, formulas, sorting/filtering, SUM/IF, XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP basics, pivot tables, CSV files
skills.depthComment: Very useful for jobs, data and freelancing.

skills.whatToLearn: What cloud means, servers, storage, databases, regions, public/private cloud, basic virtual networks
skills.depthComment: Just understand the concepts now. AWS/GCP/Azure depth can come later.

skills.whatToLearn: pwd, cd, ls, mkdir, copying/deleting files, paths, permissions, installing packages
skills.depthComment: Enough that the terminal doesn't scare her.

skills.whatToLearn: Open folders/projects, create files, extensions, terminal, running code, debugging basics
skills.depthComment: This becomes her main coding workspace.

skills.whatToLearn: Variables, data types, if/else, loops, functions, input/output, basic problem solving
skills.depthComment: Teach the logic before language syntax.

skills.whatToLearn: Variables, strings, lists, dictionaries, loops, functions, files, errors, libraries, basic OOP, simple automation
skills.depthComment: Main programming language. Spend the most time here.

skills.whatToLearn: Tables, rows, columns, primary/foreign keys, SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, relationships
skills.depthComment: Treat SQL + PostgreSQL as one subject. No need to learn multiple databases now.

skills.whatToLearn: Repository, clone, commit, push, pull, branches basics, README, uploading projects
skills.depthComment: Extremely important for future portfolio and jobs.

skills.whatToLearn: HTML structure, headings, forms, links, images, CSS layout/styling
skills.depthComment: Only enough to understand how websites work. AI can help heavily later.

skills.whatToLearn: Variables, functions, arrays/objects, events, DOM and fetch()
skills.depthComment: Keep it basic. Python remains her main language.

skills.whatToLearn: JSON objects/arrays, request/response, GET/POST, endpoints, status codes, API keys
skills.depthComment: Very important because modern apps and AI tools communicate through APIs.

skills.whatToLearn: Send GET/POST requests, headers, body, authorization and inspect responses
skills.depthComment: Small subject but extremely useful for understanding APIs.

skills.whatToLearn: Combine Python + PostgreSQL + API + simple webpage
skills.depthComment: This is where everything starts connecting together.

skills.whatToLearn: GitHub → Vercel, deploy a simple website/app, environment variables, production vs local
skills.depthComment: To teach how to put something online for world to use.

skills.whatToLearn: Container, image, Dockerfile, ports, why containers are useful
skills.depthComment: Conceptual/basic level only. No advanced DevOps.

skills.whatToLearn: Passwords, MFA, phishing, permissions, API keys, secrets, HTTPS, basic encryption concepts
skills.depthComment: Every IT person should understand this.

skills.whatToLearn: Ask AI to explain code, generate small pieces, debug errors, review code and document projects
skills.depthComment: Use AI throughout—but she must understand what the generated code is doing.

skills.whatToLearn: Read files, process Excel/CSV, call APIs, automate repetitive tasks, simple AI integrations
skills.depthComment: Excellent final stage because it combines almost everything she learned.

universities.name: Virtual University (BS Computer Science)
universities.cityMode: Remote / online, can stay in Hyderabad
universities.bestIf: You want the cheapest serious degree and maximum flexibility
universities.cost: VU shows Rs 7,000 initial payable for new students; BSCS is a formal program and VU says it aligns with HEC undergraduate policy.
universities.extraCost: Very low. Mostly internet + laptop + exam/travel to center if needed.
universities.admissionTiming: Spring 2026 admissions stay open until Apr 5, 2026.
universities.supportSelf: Yes, best option for this. She can freelance, tutor, do internships, online certifications, GitHub, portfolio work alongside study.
universities.futureValue: Good enough if she keeps grades + skills strong.
universities.verdict: Best overall for your stated goal. Cheapest, most flexible, lowest risk.

universities.name: University of Sindh – BS Computer Science
universities.bestIf: She wants a physical campus, low travel cost, and a normal university life
universities.cost: Official 2026 ad clearly shows Rs 3,000 application processing fee; it offers BS Computer Science through IMCS.
universities.extraCost: Low to medium. Since it is near Hyderabad, commute cost stays manageable and hostel may not be needed.
universities.admissionTiming: The latest official bachelor ad available is for the recent cycle; for the next main cycle, watch the admissions portal around late 2026. The university also runs an active admissions portal.
universities.supportSelf: Partly yes. Easier than Karachi options because she can stay at home and upskill online.
universities.verdict: Best nearby physical option. If she wants campus plus low cost, this is the strongest local choice.

universities.name: AIOU – BS Computer Science (ODL)
universities.bestIf: She wants a remote degree but prefers a more traditional open-university setup
universities.cost: AIOU Spring 2026 fee sheet lists BS Computer Science ODL at Rs 34,230; eligibility is Intermediate with Mathematics and at least 50% marks.
universities.extraCost: Low. Mostly internet, books, local exam/travel costs.
universities.admissionTiming: AIOU academic calendar shows Autumn admissions run from Jul 1 to Sep 5, so that is the next clean future window after Apr 3, 2026.
universities.supportSelf: Yes. Good for self-study plus side work.
universities.verdict: Second-best remote choice after VU, but for pure tech/CS image and modern perception, I’d still put VU slightly ahead.

universities.name: MUET (Software / Computer Systems / related computing paths)
universities.bestIf: She is academically stronger and wants a more technical engineering-style degree
universities.cost: MUET’s official fee page shows Rs 38,540 total admission fees under the regular scheme; MUET offers Computer Systems Engineering and Software Engineering.
universities.extraCost: Low to medium, because location is still near Hyderabad.
universities.admissionTiming: The latest official undergrad deadline was in Feb 2026; for the next cycle, watch MUET admissions in early 2027 or next announced intake.
universities.supportSelf: Partly, but workload is heavier than VU/AIOU.
universities.verdict: Great option if she can handle harder academics. But for your “cheapest + skill-first” strategy, I would still rank it below VU and Sindh.

universities.name: NED University – BS Computer Science
universities.bestIf: She is strong enough for merit and can manage Karachi travel/relocation
universities.cost: NED’s Fall 2026 undergraduate admissions page is live, and NED also has an HEC need-based scholarship route that can cover actual tuition plus Rs 6,000/month stipend for 10 months.
universities.extraCost: Medium to high for her because Karachi transport/hostel/food can add cost if not commuting from family support.
universities.admissionTiming: Fall 2026 admissions are open on the official NED page now.
universities.supportSelf: Not ideal unless family can cover base costs.
universities.verdict: Strong university, but for her specific low-cost Hyderabad case, it is not the smartest first choice unless she gets scholarship/strong merit.

scholarshipRankings.universities: Middle East Technical University (METU), Izmir Institute of Technology (IYTE)
scholarshipRankings.studyCost: About $1,800–$2,700/year for typical public-engineering/science examples before scholarship.
scholarshipRankings.livingCost: About $460–$810/month using a common €400–€700 student-living band.
scholarshipRankings.canSupportSelf: Partly. Undergrads can work only after the first year, and permit rules apply.
scholarshipRankings.admissionDates: Jan–Feb 2027 likely; the latest official cycle ran 10 Jan–20 Feb 2026.
scholarshipRankings.comments: Best overall realistic target: strong scholarship package, solid universities, and good balance of cost and future value.

scholarshipRankings.universities: University of Debrecen, Budapest University of Technology and Economics (BME)
scholarshipRankings.studyCost: Tuition can be fully covered; official support includes HUF 43,700/month stipend and free dorm or HUF 40,000/month housing contribution, which is about $132/month stipend and $121/month housing support at current rates.
scholarshipRankings.livingCost: Real student living is often still around $450–$750/month, especially if not in dorms.
scholarshipRankings.canSupportSelf: Yes, partly. Student work is possible and commonly used to fill the gap.
scholarshipRankings.admissionDates: Late 2026 to mid-Jan 2027 likely; latest official deadline was 15 Jan 2026.
scholarshipRankings.comments: Very practical Europe option. Not always fully zero-cost, but one of the best realistic scholarship routes.

scholarshipRankings.universities: Nanjing University of Information Science & Technology, Hefei University of Technology
scholarshipRankings.studyCost: Typical STEM bachelor tuition examples are about $2,300–$3,050/year before scholarship. Official undergrad stipend is CNY 2,500/month, about $363/month at current rates.
scholarshipRankings.livingCost: Varies by city, but scholarship usually covers most basics; I would still assume some personal top-up money may be needed.
scholarshipRankings.canSupportSelf: Low to medium. I would not choose this route mainly for part-time income.
scholarshipRankings.admissionDates: Late 2026 to early Jan 2027 likely; latest HEC deadline was 5 Jan 2026.
scholarshipRankings.comments: Strong for CS/STEM and more realistic than elite Western options, but less flexible than Turkey/Hungary for self-support.

scholarshipRankings.universities: Universiti Brunei Darussalam (UBD), Universiti Teknologi Brunei (UTB)
scholarshipRankings.studyCost: UBD examples are about $2,339/year for many first degrees, $2,729/year for lab-based first degrees, and about $7,016/year for engineering before scholarship.
scholarshipRankings.canSupportSelf: No. Paid employment is generally not allowed during the scholarship.
scholarshipRankings.admissionDates: Early 2027 likely; the 2026/27 scholarship page is live, but the public page I found did not clearly show the closing date.
scholarshipRankings.comments: Very good fully funded route for CS because UBD lists programs such as Computer Science, Data Science, AI, and Cybersecurity-related areas, but weak for students who need to work during study.

scholarshipRankings.studyCost: Tuition is covered under the scholarship, but the main issue is language. Before scholarship, Romania is one of the cheaper EU study destinations.
scholarshipRankings.livingCost: Roughly $115–$346/month for food alone, with total student spending often still moderate by EU standards.
scholarshipRankings.canSupportSelf: Yes, partly. Non-EU students can work while studying.
scholarshipRankings.admissionDates: Feb–Mar 2027 likely; the 2026 cycle ran 16 Feb–31 Mar 2026.
scholarshipRankings.comments: Biggest drawback: for this scholarship, bachelor’s study is mainly attractive only if the student is comfortable with Romanian-medium study or a preparatory Romanian year.

scholarshipRankings.universities: University of Tsukuba, Institute of Science Tokyo
scholarshipRankings.studyCost: Before scholarship, official annual tuition is about $5,141 at national universities, $5,705 at local public, and about $8,150 at private universities. MEXT gives ¥117,000/month stipend plus tuition exemption and airfare.
scholarshipRankings.livingCost: Official average living cost is about $658/month, and average housing is about $257/month nationally.
scholarshipRankings.canSupportSelf: Partly, but not enough to fully self-fund. Part-time work helps, but Japan’s own guidance says students should not assume it will fully cover everything.
scholarshipRankings.admissionDates: Watch Apr–May 2026 for the next embassy round; Pakistan’s last posted undergrad deadline for the previous cycle was 31 May 2025.
scholarshipRankings.comments: Excellent scholarship and strong long-term value, but for an average student it is usually harder than Turkey, Hungary, or China.
